options: The report loads in under 3 seconds for 100,000 rows
The interface must be user friendly
why: A testable requirement has a measurable condition. 'Fast' and 'friendly' can't fail a test.

q: In a data model, a foreign key:
options: Links a row in one table to a row in another
why: It expresses a relationship, such as each record belonging to an entity, and lets the database reject orphans.

q: As server utilisation approaches 100%, average waiting time in a queue:
why: Queues are non-linear. Running at 95% utilisation produces long waits, which is why you size for headroom.

q: Net present value discounts future cash flows because:
options: Money received later is worth less than money today
It makes the project look worse on purpose
why: A dollar today can be invested. Discounting puts all cash flows on the same footing.

q: TELOS feasibility covers which five dimensions?
why: Scoring each dimension shows the weakest one before you commit.

q: A traceability matrix links each requirement to:
options: The design and test that prove it was met
why: It shows which requirements have no test and which tests cover no requirement.

q: What should a problem statement describe?
options: The solution you plan to build
The problem and who is affected, so any proposal can be judged against it
why: Writing the solution instead of the problem makes it impossible to tell whether another solution would work better.

q: You can speed up any step of a process. Which one should you work on?
options: The bottleneck, the step that limits the whole flow
why: Speeding up a step that is not the bottleneck does not change the end-to-end time.

q: Three systems all store customer addresses and none is designated the master. What is the problem?
options: The copies will drift and nobody knows which is right
why: Without one system of record, each copy can be changed separately and you cannot say which version to trust.

q: Which best describes a single source of truth?
options: One designated owner system per piece of information, with other systems copying from it
why: It is about ownership of each piece of information, not about putting everything in one product.

q: A metric appears in a report but supports no decision and has no owner. What should you do?
options: Name the decision and an owner, or drop it
why: Data should support action. A number nobody owns or uses is noise.

q: Which file name is the biggest warning sign?
why: Version words in a name mean nobody knows which copy is current. Keep the version in a field.

q: Why ask 'if the compliance manager left tomorrow, what would happen?'
options: It reveals whether knowledge is documented and shared or held by one person
why: Compliance systems should work without any one individual. The answer shows how fragile they are.

q: 40 people each search for documents 3 times a day for 8 minutes. What is wrong with quoting the yearly cost?
options: It is only as good as the guesses; time a real retrieval test first
why: The arithmetic is easy, but the inputs are estimates. Measure a sample before presenting the number.
